plan.area: AREA 1 — the doctrine prior: a cost-effectiveness table derived from CFG.DMG, the penetration model, the weapon table and unit costs, cached per faction+era, meeting counterMix() as a modulator on its existing hand-tuned coefficients.
plan.summary: I derived, in jsc, an expected-value-per-credit table for every role a faction can build in an era against each of the five armour classes, from CFG.DMG, CFG.PEN_PER_DMG / PEN_NONE / PEN_FULL, the weapon table (dmg, warhead, pen, range, reload, burst, acc, tgt) and P.factionCost, folding in our own army's published accMul / rangeMul / ammoQ / costMul. It reproduces every obvious truth: flak leads the air column for every army (130.8 per 1,000 credits for a Stinger team), heat leads the heavy column for every army (Javelin 64.2 vs Abrams 22.7), bullet leads the infantry column for every army (MG team 134-236), and HE leads structures — the nuance being that the only he weapon in the ground order of battle is the ballistic launcher, so among the fifteen manoeuvre roles counterMix actually buys, the best structure multiplier available is heat at 0.80 and frag at 0.75, and the column is led by heat carriers accordingly. The shipped output is not the raw table but one normalised number per role per class: this army's share of its own buyable answer to that class, over the share a typical army of the period puts there. An unremarkable army scores 1.00 everywhere and counterMix behaves exactly as today; only the unusual armies move. Cold build 0.44 ms per faction+era including the eight-army norm, 73 ns a lookup after that. It MODULATES counterMix rather than replacing it, which is what keeps test [29] passing and its adaptation intact.
plan.design:
WHAT IS PRICED, per weapon, per target class:
  dps          = dmg * burst * clamp(acc * faction.accMul, 0.03, 0.98) / cycle,
                 cycle = max(0.5, reload + burst*burstDelay). Same derivation
                 gunProfile() at ai.js:71-73 already uses, so the two readings
                 in the file agree about the same gun.
  warhead      CFG.dmgMult(warhead, class), unmodified.
  penetration  pen (declared, or dmg * CFG.PEN_PER_DMG[warhead], with the same
               ammoQ fallback bonus penOf() applies at combat.js:802) against
               an era-typical reference plate, through the identical
               PEN_NONE 0.72 / PEN_FULL 1.00 linear ramp resolveArmor uses at
               combat.js:829-836. Applied ONLY to the heavy and light classes,
               because resolveArmor returns null for infantry, structures and
               aircraft — they get the flat matrix, exactly as in the engine.
  tgt mask     a flak mount is not in a tank's war, a cannon is not in an
               aeroplane's. Decisive and invisible unless you read it: this is
               what catches the Starstreak below.
  reach        0.75 + 0.25 * clamp(range * rangeMul / 8, 0, 3). Anchored so a
               tank gun at 8 tiles is exactly 1.00, the same construction
               CFG.ASPECT_MUL uses for the frontal arc. A 23-tile MLRS gets
               1.47, a 6-tile nest 0.94. Mild on purpose — a tiebreaker, not
               the argument.
  cost         Math.round(cost * faction.costMul) — value per CREDIT is the
               question, and NATO's 1.06 is a real 6% tax on every purchase.
  ammoQ        the damage side too (heavy x ammoQ, light x 1+(ammoQ-1)*0.5),
               matching applyDamage at combat.js:891-896.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, and why:
  aspect / ricochet  ASPECT_MUL front is 1.00 by construction. Pricing the
                     frontal arc prices the trade a PURCHASE guarantees; a
                     flank multiplier prices a manoeuvre, and a queue cannot
                     buy a manoeuvre. Ricochet needs obliq > 66 deg and a
                     head-on shot at a 52-deg glacis is 52, so it never fires
                     frontally anyway.
  area of effect     an M270 pod is aoe 2.0 with burst 12; what that is worth
                     depends on how the enemy is spaced, which is a SIGHTING.
                     So the prior does not touch the spg/mlrs terms at all and
                     they keep their hand-argued reach basis.
  suppression        the mg term in counterMix is argued from SUPPRESS_BREAK 86
                     against fourteen rounds at 30 suppression each, not from
                     damage. Damage is not what shifts a squad in cover, so a
                     damage table cannot price the machine gun and must not
                     pretend to. (This is why the infantry modulators all come
                     out 0.88-1.15 — the table correctly finds nothing to say.)
  survivability      the 400-credit Javelin team is the best anti-armour value
                     per credit in EVERY army in EVERY era. An army of nothing
                     but Javelin teams loses to a rifle company. This is the
                     single strongest argument for modulating rather than
                     replacing, and for the clamp and the guard() floor.
  sustained-rate bias the metric is a rate, so it undervalues one-shot
                     weapons: a TEL scores 2.5-4.2 per 1,000 credits against
                     structures where a Javelin team scores 37.5. Another
                     reason the prior is confined to the direct-fire counter
                     sets counterMix trades in.

NORMALISATION — the key design choice. A raw per-credit number is not
comparable across categories (infantry weapons always win; a first attempt
saturated the clamp at 1.80 for `at` and 0.55 for `mortar` for all eight
armies, which differentiates nothing). So the shipped modulator is
  share_this_army(role, class) / mean_share_over_the_period's_eight_armies
computed within each counter set. "Every army's AT team is cheap" cancels out;
what survives is exactly "THIS army's ATGM is unusually good / its tank gun
unusually bad", which is the stated goal. Clamped [0.55, 1.80] so the prior can
shift emphasis but never invent or delete a role.

ONE HARD RULE THAT IS NOT A SHARE: if a role's value against a class is zero —
the weapon cannot engage it at all — the modulator is 0, not the clamp floor.
That is the same fact gunProfile() already acts on when it throws away a SAM
site's weapon, and it is what makes the British air-defence finding actionable.

CACHE: doctrine(fac, era) on the key fac+"|"+era. doctPlate(era) walks only the
five armour role lists (37 in-era hulls at e20, not 1,202 units); doctValue
touches at most eleven units. Nothing per-match ever enters it — no upgrades,
no veterancy, no optics — so the key stays sound.

MEETS counterMix() BY MODULATING, NOT REPLACING. Reasons, in order:
 1. Test [29] asserts at2<at1, td2<td1, mg2>mg1 as the observed shares move.
    Every one of those terms is `coefficient * observed_share * grip * ...`.
    Multiplying by a constant-within-a-match modulator preserves the
    monotonicity in `armour` and `foot` EXACTLY. Replacing the coefficients
    with absolute prior-derived values would put the sign and magnitude
    relationships the test proves at the mercy of the derivation.
 2. The hand constants know things the prior structurally cannot see:
    suppression, reach against a prepared position, aps 0.40-0.45 against
    missiles, and a thin hull dying in a defended base. The prior knows the
    ammunition; the constants know the war. Replacing throws the war away.
 3. It is the smaller, more legible diff — nine multiplications and one
    lookup, in a file somebody has to read in a year.
 4. The adaptation does not weaken, it sharpens: the modulator scales the
    RESPONSE to an observed share, so a bigger modulator makes the same
    sighting move the queue FURTHER, not less.
The two ifv/lighttank DISCOUNTS are modulated as `clamp(2 - mod, ...)` so a
role the prior rates highly gets a smaller discount — mod 1.00 reproduces
today's 0.35 and 0.70 exactly.

NOT IN THIS AREA, on purpose: the standing floor mixture at the top of
counterMix. Shaping the floor by the prior is the natural next step and would
be the real "starts competent instead of ignorant" win, but it changes the
opening of every match and is the largest behavioural change in the file — it
deserves its own measurement pass.
plan.coldStart:
For the first several minutes seenU is empty, so a.sArmour, a.sInf, a.sLight and a.sArty are all 0, a.air is 0 and a.line is 0 — not one of counterMix's counter blocks fires. The commander builds the floor mixture, exactly as it does today. Every modulator multiplies a term that is already gated on an observed share, so THE PRIOR CHANGES NOTHING WHILE THE PLOT IS EMPTY. That is deliberate and it is the honest reading of the owner's two requests together: the prior says what to build GIVEN what was seen, and the seeing is still the thing that has to happen first.

What actually runs in the first three minutes: nothing at all until the first sighting reaches counterMix past the grip>0 gate, at which point doctrine(P.faction, P.era) builds in 0.44 ms on one think() tick and every call after that is a property read at 73 ns. There is no warm-up, no sampling and no state — the table is a pure function of the two static tables and is correct on its first use.

The one visible cold-start effect is negative and intended: a commander whose army has a zero-value role against a class (the British SHORAD below) stops adding weight to it the moment it sees an aircraft, instead of buying MANPADS that cannot hurt one. Its floor share of 0.12 aa survives, because the floor is out of scope here.
plan.fogAudit:
Every input to the prior, and where it comes from:

  CFG.DMG, CFG.dmgMult                     config.js, static constant
  CFG.PEN_PER_DMG, PEN_NONE, PEN_FULL,
    PEN_FAIL_MUL, PEN_WARHEADS,
    ARMOR_MM, ARMOR_HP_REF                 config.js, static constant
  WEAPONS[k].dmg / warhead / pen / range /
    reload / burst / burstDelay / acc / tgt rules.js + eras.js + generations.js,
                                           the published weapon table — the same
                                           card the player reads in the sidebar
  UNITS[k].cost / hp / armor / armorMM /
    weapons / from / to                    the published unit table, same
  FACTIONS[OUR faction].accMul, rangeMul,
    costMul, ammoQ                         rules.js:279, OUR OWN army's modifiers
  P.faction, P.era                         OUR OWN player object
  ROLES, unitFor(), inEra()                the role index over the same tables

NOT READ, ANYWHERE IN THIS CHANGE: no game object, no map, no tile, no seenB,
no seenU, no look grid, no dossier, no enemy player, no enemy queue, no enemy
cash, no enemy unit list. doctrine() takes (fac, era) — two strings — and can
be called with no Game at all; that is how the jsc harness runs it.

THE ONE THING THAT NEEDS SAYING OUT LOUD. The era norm is a mean over all eight
armies' published rosters for that decade. That is NOT a peek at the opponent:
it is a normalisation constant computed from static tables, it says nothing
about which armies are in this match or where anything is, and the same number
comes out whether the commander is fighting one opponent or five. It is the
same class of thing as GUNS and AAG at module level, which the file already
justifies as "the recognition manual, and it is the same manual the human
reads". Comparing your own army against the period's armies is precisely what
a staff college teaches. If that is still felt to be one step too far, the
fallback is to normalise against the flat 1/N — I measured it, and it saturates
the clamp for every faction and differentiates nothing, which is why it is not
what I am proposing.

The OBSERVED half stays where it is and is untouched: a.sArmour / a.sInf /
a.sLight / a.sArty / a.air / a.line all still come from seenU and seenB through
foeArms(), and heatEdge(a.plate) still asks the observed-plate question against
our own gun. The prior is a coefficient on those terms, never a substitute for
them. The reference plate inside the prior is era-typical and deliberately not
the observed plate, precisely so that the cache key can stay (faction, era) and
so that nothing about a sighting can leak into a module-level table shared
between commanders.

risks: A LIVE CONTENT BUG, NOT AN AI BUG, surfaced by the derivation: Starstreak HVM declares warhead "cannon" and CFG.DMG.cannon.air is 0.00, so the Starstreak Team (400cr) and the Stormer HVM (980cr) - the whole of Britain's ground-based air defence at e90 and e20 - do literally zero damage to an aircraft in applyDamage today, with or without this change. The same check flags France's AMX-10P 20mm, which declares tgt.air with warhead "cannon". The prior handles it correctly by refusing to spend on them, but the real fix is a warhead of "flak" in eras.js, and that is a balance decision for you, not for me. If you fix it, both British modulators move from 0.00 to a normal share on the next load with no AI change needed.

THE HARD-ZERO RULE IS THE ONE PLACE THE PRIOR CAN SILENCE A PURCHASE. It fires only when a role's value against a class is exactly 0 - the weapon cannot engage it at all - and today it fires for exactly two entries (gbr aa, gbr spaag). If a future weapon is added with a warhead whose matrix entry is 0 against its declared tgt class, the prior will silently stop buying it. That is the correct answer, but it will look like the AI has decided to ignore a unit. The diagnostic is AI.doctValueOf(fac, era) showing a 0 in that column.

THE ERA NORM READS ALL EIGHT ARMIES' STATIC TABLES. I argue in the fog audit that this is doctrine and not intelligence - it is a normalisation constant over published rosters, identical whether the commander faces one opponent or five, and it contains no position, no sighting and no quantity. If you disagree, the fallback is to normalise against a flat 1/N, and I measured that: it saturates the clamp at 1.80 for `at` and 0.55 for `mortar` for every single army in every era, differentiating nothing. There is no third option that both differentiates and reads only one roster.

ADDING A FACTION MOVES EVERY OTHER FACTION'S MODULATORS. The norm is a mean over eight; a ninth army with an extreme roster shifts it by roughly an eighth. The effect is small and self-correcting, but it means the printed tables in the comment block will drift as eras.js grows. They are stated as measured numbers with a date-free "as the tables stand", and the jsc harness reprints them in under a second - re-run it after any weapon or unit change and update the comment if a headline figure has moved.

THE METRIC IS A SUSTAINED RATE AND UNDERVALUES ONE-SHOT WEAPONS. A TEL scores 2.5-4.2 per 1,000 credits against structures where a Javelin team scores 37.5, purely because of its reload. This is why DOCT_SET deliberately excludes tel, spg, mlrs, sniper and radarv, and why the prior never touches the artillery or counterbattery terms. If somebody later adds spg or mlrs to DOCT_SET without adding an area-of-effect term, the prior will start arguing against artillery and it will be wrong.

THE REFERENCE PLATE IS ERA-TYPICAL, NOT OBSERVED, ON PURPOSE - it is what lets the cache key be (faction, era) and lets the table sit at module level shared between commanders. The observed half of the anti-armour argument lives entirely in heatEdge(a.plate), which this change leaves alone. If heatEdge is ever removed or neutered, the anti-armour weighting loses its fogged half and becomes pure doctrine, which is exactly the failure the owner is worried about. The two must stay coupled.

NOTHING PER-MATCH MAY EVER ENTER doctValue(). No upgrades (optics is a 1.15 on range), no veterancy, no supply strain, no weather - the moment one does, the (faction, era) cache key is wrong and two commanders of the same nation will silently share one commander's state. The functions take (fac, era) and nothing else specifically so this is hard to get wrong by accident.

I HAVE NOT SHAPED THE STANDING FLOOR MIXTURE, which is the largest remaining win and the thing that would most directly answer "start the commander competent instead of ignorant". A British commander still carries 0.12 aa in its floor for weapons that cannot hurt an aircraft. Doing it is a one-line change per floor entry and test [29] would survive it (the test only asserts directions, and a per-faction constant on the floor preserves all three), but it changes the opening of every match for every army and deserves its own measurement pass rather than riding in on this one.

problems.item: js/ai.js ~1660 edit: veh.lighttank *= 1 - 0.70 * armour * grip * U.clamp(2 - dm.heavy.lighttank, 0.2, 1.30)

problems.reality: The shipped modulator anti-correlates with the value table it is derived from. I ran the proposed counterMix with and without dm (KPA e20, armour 0.80, tech 3, grip 1, heat 0.9, then normalised the vehicle queue the way buildToward does): lighttank 0.040 -> 0.079 (NEARLY DOUBLE) for a role the proposal's own table prices at 2.4 EV/1,000cr against heavy, while tankdestroyer (5.5) falls 0.172 -> 0.152 and inf.at (14.5) falls 0.360 -> 0.337. NATO e20 identical in shape: lighttank 0.040 -> 0.075 (11.0 EV) while tankdestroyer (25.4) 0.172 -> 0.149 and inf.at (64.2) 0.360 -> 0.333. Cause: share/era-mean-share measures "how much of MY OWN army's anti-tank total sits here", not "is this a good buy", and the lighttank era-mean share is tiny (0.039 at e20) so noise is amplified — KPA lighttank 2.4 EV scores 1.73 while PACT lighttank 2.0 EV scores 0.68, a 2.5x spread between two roles within 20% of each other, driven entirely by the DENOMINATOR (KPA tot 36.5 vs PACT tot 74.1). A weak army inflates every one of its own roles. In the flagship KPA case the prior demotes the single best anti-armour weapon it owns and promotes the second-worst.

problems.item: js/ai.js doctrine(): const share = tot > 0 ? v[role][c] / tot : 0, where tot sums only roles this army can build

problems.reality: Confounded with roster gaps. Because tot loses the missing role's term, every surviving role's share inflates. France's raw AT value is 56.5 EV/1,000cr — LOWER than NATO's 64.2 — yet France scores 1.53 and NATO 0.77. The gap also inflates the AGGREGATE response, because the missing role still returns modulator 1 and still gets its full 0.30 coefficient added: mean heavy-set modulator is FRA e20 1.16 and DEU e20 1.19 against PACT e20 0.90, and since buildToward normalises within the vehicle queue that extra mass is taken straight out of spg/mlrs/spaag, which the proposal says it does not touch.

The light set contains only lighttank and at, there is no mbt term in it, and the light block (guarded by light > 0.40 && armour < 0.15) adds no mbt at all. Nothing in the shipped change lets the commander buy the Chonma-ho as a carrier-killer. The discount edit reads dm.heavy.lighttank, not dm.light.lighttank, so the anti-carrier reading is not what modulates it either.

problems.item: js/ai.js ~1640 edits: add(inf, "mg", 0.22 * foot * grip * dm.infantry.mg) and the matching mortar term
problems.claim: "modulated for consistency"; the proposal states the result is 0.88-1.24 for all eight armies in both eras and that a damage table cannot price suppression anyway.
problems.reality: Confirmed 0.883-1.151 across 8 factions x 6 eras. These two multiplications are admitted no-ops that buy nothing and add a failure surface on the two terms test [29] asserts on. If the infantry column has nothing to say, the honest form is to leave the lines alone and say so in the comment, not to multiply by a number the design already argues is meaningless.

missed: The normaliser is the whole decision and there is no ablation against the obvious alternative. share/era-mean-share was compared only against a flat 1/N (which the proposal correctly rejects). It was never compared against the normaliser that actually matches the stated goal — value-per-credit for THIS army's role over the era-mean value-per-credit for THAT SAME role across the eight rosters. That one is immune to both defects above: it has no per-army denominator, so a weak army cannot inflate its own worst role, and a missing role simply drops out of one column instead of rescaling every other. It would have given KPA lighttank ~0.4 and NATO lighttank ~1.8 off the same numbers, which is the answer the table actually contains.

No guard that the modulator agrees in sign with the value it came from. A one-line assertion in the behaviour suite — for each army and era, the highest-modulator role in the heavy set is not one whose EV/1,000cr is below the set median — would have caught the lighttank inversion before it was written up as a feature. As shipped the only test coverage is test [29], which is insensitive to any constant factor and therefore cannot see this class of error at all.

The aggregate effect on the queue is never measured. Every number in priorTable is a per-role modulator; nothing in the proposal shows what counterMix's output actually becomes. Because buildToward normalises within each category (js/ai.js:1737-1748), a modulator set whose mean is above 1 moves credits out of the unmodulated artillery and air-defence terms in the same queue. That is a real behavioural change in the spg/mlrs/spaag mix which the design explicitly claims not to touch.

The heavy/light reference plate is derived from u.hp, but combat.js armorAt (js/combat.js:779-788) scales from e.maxHp, which carries the owner's FACTIONS.hpMul (0.86 KPA to 1.08 PACT/GBR). The prior therefore prices every army's shot against a plate 7-14% thinner or thicker than the one resolveArmor will actually present. It does not change the ordering at e20 (738mm is far above every gun's PEN_NONE threshold for the armies that bounce) but it is an unflagged divergence from the engine in a derivation whose entire claim is that it agrees with the engine.

doctValue silently prices only weapons[0..n] with no minRange term, while the file's own gunProfile keeps minRange because coast_gun and bunker_how are dead inside it. Nothing in the manoeuvre roles currently declares a minRange that matters, but the omission is undocumented in a block that documents everything else it leaves out.

problems.item: doctNorm(era) / doctPlate(era) — the cross-faction reads (ai.js new module block)
problems.claim: fogAudit: "NOT READ, ANYWHERE IN THIS CHANGE: ... no enemy player ... no enemy unit list" and "The era norm is a mean over all eight armies' published rosters for that decade. That is NOT a peek at the opponent."
problems.reality: VERIFIED AND I AGREE THAT NOTHING MATCH-DEPENDENT LEAKS, but the charter line I was given is "the commander's OWN buildable roster is legitimate", and this code reads every other army's roster too. doctNorm calls doctValue(fac, era) for all of Object.keys(FACTIONS) = nato,pact,pla,kpa,roc,gbr,fra,deu (verified in jsc), and doctPlate takes a median over ALL in-era hulls off ROLES, not just ours (e60 heavy 161mm, e20 heavy 738mm — I reproduced both exactly). The operational test clears it: I ran doctrine() in jsc with no Game, no map, no player and no opponent, and the output is a pure function of (faction, era) — identical whether the AI faces KPA, NATO or five opponents at once, so no information about THIS match can flow through it. The one place it is a hair better than an own-roster-only prior is that a KPA commander learns foreign plate is thicker than its own; that is open-source reference data, the same class as the GUNS/AAG precedent the file already justifies. Note the distinction from that precedent, though, and it is the reason this needs the owner's explicit yes: GUNS/AAG are lookups KEYED BY A SIGHTING (gunProfile(r.key) is only ever called on a seenB record); doctNorm/doctPlate are unconditional aggregates over everybody. Cheap proof that it carries no intelligence: both could be frozen into the file as literal constants with byte-identical behaviour. If the owner wants the charter read literally, freeze them; do not switch to flat 1/N (the author is right that it saturates).

problems.item: the aa/spaag edit's justification, and coldStart's "a British commander correctly stops buying them"
problems.claim: edit why: "it stops spending on them" / "until it is fixed, not buying them is correct"
problems.reality: dm.air.aa = 0 only zeroes the OBSERVED-air increment add(inf,"aa", 0.16*air*grip*0). The standing floor inf.aa = 0.12 is explicitly out of scope, so a British commander goes on buying Starstreak teams at the floor share — and worse, because air>0 takes the `if` branch, it keeps the full 0.12 when aircraft ARE seen and decays to 0.06 when they are not, i.e. the prior makes Britain's air-defence buying slightly ANTI-correlated with the air picture. The underlying content bug is real and I confirmed it independently: gbr aa/spaag from e90 onward are w_e*_gbr_aa/spaag warhead "cannon", CFG.DMG.cannon.air = 0.00, and applyDamage bails at `if (dmg <= 0.5) return` (combat.js:947) — literally nothing. 11 of 312 air-only weapons in the roster have this defect. Britain is not disarmed by the zero (its `sam` role is Rapier FSC / Sky Sabre, warhead flak, and sam_site/aa_battery are flak), so the substitution argument holds — only the claim about what the commander stops buying is overstated.

problems.item: the two modulated discounts, veh.lighttank *= 1 - 0.70*armour*grip*U.clamp(2-dm,0.2,1.30)
problems.claim: "Clamped [0.55, 1.80] so the prior can shift emphasis but never invent or delete a role" / "a modulator between 0.55 and 1.80 can shift emphasis but can never invent a role or delete one."
problems.reality: True on the six add() paths, false on the discount paths, which is where the clamp is inverted. At dm 0.55-0.68 the factor is 1.30 and the light-tank cut rises from 0.70 to 0.91: with armour=1 and grip=1, veh.lighttank keeps 0.076 of its 0.12 floor (PACT e20 lighttank is 0.68 → 0.091x; GBR e20 is 0.55 → 0.076x), and if the `line` block also fires it compounds to ~0.036x. guard() protects ["mbt","ifv"] at tech>=2, not lighttank, so the role is effectively deleted rather than de-emphasised. Defensible as a decision (a Sprut-SD really does score 1.95 per 1,000 credits against an e20 heavy) but the stated invariant should not claim otherwise.

problems.item: the normalisation, for armies with a missing role in a counter set
problems.claim: "An unremarkable army scores 1.00 everywhere and counterMix behaves exactly as today; only the unusual armies move" — the modulator is presented as re-splitting the response.
problems.reality: The share denominator is summed only over roles the army HAS, while the norm is a per-role mean over the armies that have it, so an army with a gap gets every surviving role inflated together. Measured in jsc, the mean modulator over the armour set: fra e60 1.41 (missing tankdestroyer and heavy), deu e20 1.19 (missing heavy and lighttank), fra e20 1.16, gbr e20 1.07, against nato e60 0.90 and pact e20 0.90. Since buildToward normalises want[role]/sum across ALL roles including the unmodulated floor, a mean of 1.41 does not just re-split the anti-armour response, it moves the whole queue off the floor toward counters for France specifically — an artifact of role-set size, not a doctrinal fact about France. The design never mentions this; if it is wanted, say so; if not, divide each set's modulators by their own mean so the prior is split-preserving.

problems.item: const dm = doctrine(P.faction, P.era || CUR_ERA); (and the same expression in the intel() edit)
problems.claim: fogAudit: "P.faction, P.era — OUR OWN player object"
problems.reality: P.era is our own and is always set (game.js:87 `p.era = isHuman ? G.era : G.eraAI`), so today this is honest. But the fallback is not neutral: game.js:11 sets CUR_ERA to the HUMAN's era ('CUR_ERA ... follows the human'), and mixed-era battles are a supported mode (G.era vs G.eraAI). Any future path that reaches counterMix with P.era unset — a synthetic player in a harness, a save restored without era — silently hands the commander the human's period, which would set the reference plate from the enemy's generation. The file's existing idiom passes bare P.era and lets unitFor fall back, so this carries the same latent hazard; prefer bare P.era here, or G.eraAI.

problems.item: the last edit (AI API: doctrineOf)
problems.claim: "A module-level entry point so the manual can be printed for ANY faction and era from the browser console"
problems.reality: The proposal text is truncated mid-literal (`return doctrine(fac, era || C`), so I could not verify its body, its anchor repetition or its brace balance — the one rule this project has lost ten edits to. Its anchor (the intelOf/personalities block) counts exactly 1 in js/ai.js. Separately, worth stating on purpose rather than by omission: doctrineOf(fac, era) is a loaded gun for fog — it will answer for the HUMAN's faction, and nothing in ai.js may ever call it with anything but P.faction.

missed: I verified the eleven other fogAudit lines by hand and they hold. CFG.DMG / dmgMult / PEN_PER_DMG / PEN_NONE 0.72 / PEN_FULL 1.00 / PEN_FAIL_MUL 0.12 / PEN_WARHEADS / ARMOR_MM / ARMOR_HP_REF all exist in config.js as named. The penetration ramp in doctValue is line-for-line resolveArmor (combat.js:829-836); the ammoQ split (heavy x aq, light x 1+(aq-1)*0.5) is applyDamage combat.js:895; the declared-vs-derived pen rule with the 0.6 ammoQ bonus is penOf combat.js:802-803; restricting the ramp to heavy/light matches resolveArmor's `e.cat !== 'vehicle'` and armour-class guards. The observed half is untouched: foeArms() (ai.js:1228-1268) still builds sArmour/sInf/sLight/sArty/air/plate from seenU.values() and seenB.values() only, and every modulated term is still coefficient x observed share x grip, behind the grip>0 Recruit gate.

Reproduced the whole shipped modulator table in jsc from the live tables: all 8 factions x both eras match the proposal cell for cell, including gbr e20 aa 0.00 / spaag 0.00, kpa e20 ifv 1.80 / mbt 0.57, nato e20 ifv 1.35 / lighttank 1.69, pact e60 ifv 1.80, fra e20 at 1.53 / mbt 1.55, roc e20 mbt 0.55. Plates 161mm/738mm reproduce. Cost measured 0.57 ms cold (claimed 0.44) and 82 ns a cached lookup (claimed 73) — both noise-level, the claim stands.

All twelve anchors verified with python3 str.count: every one is exactly 1 in js/ai.js. No identifier collision — 'doctValue', 'doctPlate', 'doctNorm' are 0 occurrences today and the 12 hits for 'doctrine' / 3 for 'DOCT' are all comment prose ('DOCTRINE A: BUYING REACH', 'the mine doctrine'), no existing binding. Object.keys(FACTIONS) at module level is safe: rules.js loads before ai.js in index.html and reindexRoles() has already run (58 role keys present at load), and generations.js is a load-time IIFE over all factions, so no per-match table mutation can poison the cache.

Test [29] should survive, for the reason given: it asserts only monotonicity (at2<at1 && td2<td1, mg2>mg1, m1!==m2) at a fixed faction and era (_behtest sets both sides to e20), and every modulator is constant within a match and strictly positive for every faction on those four terms. The one way it could break is a modulator of exactly 0 on at/td/mg, which cannot happen — 0 requires a weapon with no tgt bit for the class at all. I did not run it; the human measures.

THE AREA SHIPS NO LEARNING AND NO EXPLORATION AT ALL, and its own coldStart says the prior 'CHANGES NOTHING WHILE THE PLOT IS EMPTY' because every modulator multiplies an already-observed share. So the half of the owner's request this area is named for — 'start competent instead of ignorant' — is deferred with the floor mixture to a later pass, and the prior is fully deterministic, adding exactly zero variety. On its own, Area 1 cannot move the 'only repetition' complaint; it is only worth shipping if the floor-shaping and the outcome loop actually land behind it.

doctValue prices whatever unitFor returns regardless of tech, prereq or P.lockReason, which is the opposite of the file's own precedent 20 lines away — hullYardstick deliberately prices only what the yard can cut TODAY, with a long comment about why. Harmless here (every modulated term is already gated on P.tech), but the inconsistency deserves a sentence or the same lockReason test.

doctPlate's comment says it is 'the same derivation armorAt() uses'; armorAt scales by e.maxHp (which carries the faction hpMul), doctPlate by the raw u.hp. Irrelevant to a period constant, but the comment claims identity it does not have.

Worth a behaviour test, since the whole point is that this table is not intelligence: assert AI.doctrineOf('gbr','e20').air.aa === 0 and AI.doctrineOf('nato','e20').heavy.ifv > 1.2 (both from static tables, no game needed), and assert that doctrine() is callable before Game.init — that pins the fog property as a regression test rather than a promise in a comment.

The Starstreak/Stormer finding is a genuine content bug and should be fixed in the weapon table rather than compensated for in ai.js, as the author says. Scope it properly first: 11 of 312 air-only weapons in the roster declare a warhead CFG.DMG scores 0.00 against air (the gbr aa/spaag families at e90/e00/e20 and France's cannon mounts among them), so a human player buying Starstreak is being sold the same nothing.

problems.item: edit 6 — veh.lighttank *= 1 - 0.70 * armour * grip * U.clamp(2 - dm.heavy.lighttank, 0.2, 1.30)  (js/ai.js:1614)
problems.claim: "A role the prior rates highly gets a smaller discount… a Bradley at 1.35 is cut 0.23; a Warrior at 0.55 is cut 0.51." The light-tank discount is modulated on the same principle as the IFV one.
problems.reality: For the light tank the modulator is INVERTED with respect to the fact it claims to carry. Measured in jsc against the live tables: NATO e20 dm.heavy.lighttank = 1.69 while the Stryker MGS is worth 11.0 per 1,000 credits against heavy — 0.17 of NATO's best answer (Javelin 64.2) and half an Abrams. KPA e20 = 1.73 on a PT-85 worth 2.45, also 0.17 of its best. ROC, whose light tank is 0.07 of its best, gets 0.80; DEU e60, 0.18 of best, gets 0.65. The correlation between the shipped modulator and the underlying value is essentially noise, and it is strongest where the underlying value is worst. Cause: the era-norm share for `lighttank` is tiny (~3.9% of the heavy set), so a small share difference makes a large ratio, and share-within-set cannot separate "my light tank is good" from "everything else of mine is terrible" — the KPA's 6.7% share exists because its whole heavy set is worthless. Running the full modulated counterMix on a normalised queue against a tank corps (sArmour 0.70, plate 738, tech 3, grip 1): NATO light tanks go 5.2% -> 8.4% of the vehicle queue and KPA 5.1% -> 8.8%. That is the commander buying ~65% more thin-skinned hulls that cannot hurt the thing they are being bought to fight, on first contact, for two of eight armies — the exact term the file's own comment installed to stop that, weakened by a number that does not mean what the edit says it means. It also contradicts the design's own stated reason for modulating rather than replacing ("the prior structurally cannot see survivability"), since this edit lets the prior overrule the one coefficient that encodes survivability. The IFV edit does NOT have this defect: dm.heavy.ifv tracks the absolute anchor in all 16 faction-era cases I measured (nato 0.47 abs -> 1.35, kpa 0.69 -> 1.80, pact 0.12 -> 0.55, gbr 0.00 -> 0.55). Fix: drop the lighttank modulation, or anchor BOTH discounts to an absolute within-army ratio value(role,heavy)/max(value in set) instead of the era-norm share — measured, that keeps every IFV case and removes both light-tank regressions.

problems.item: doctValue() penetration block — aspect/top attack deliberately excluded ("a flank multiplier prices a manoeuvre, and a queue cannot buy a manoeuvre")
problems.claim: Aspect is left out because ASPECT_MUL.front is 1.00 by construction and pricing the frontal arc prices what a purchase guarantees.
problems.reality: That argument does not apply to top attack, and top attack is the largest faction-differentiating anti-armour mechanic in the engine. combat.js:757 `if (w && w.belly) return { arc: "top", obliq: 0 }` fires unconditionally — a belly weapon ALWAYS hits the roof, so it is purchase-guaranteed, not a manoeuvre. Sixteen weapons carry it and generations.js:260-300 splits them by faction: Javelin (nato/gbr/roc), Akeron (fra), MELLS (deu), HJ-12 (pla), TOW-2B Aero (nato/roc), PARS 3 (deu) are belly; Kornet (pact) and Bulsae-3/-4 (kpa) are not. Modelled the way combat.js does it (era-typical top plate 52 mm at e20 against the 738 mm front the prior uses, times ASPECT_MUL.top 2.40), the Javelin team goes from 64.2 to 154.1 per 1,000 credits, and the shipped table moves materially for six of eight armies: pact at 0.97 -> 0.78 and pact mbt 0.85 -> 1.34, kpa at 0.79 -> 0.63, roc tankdestroyer 1.02 -> 1.35, pla at 0.81 -> 1.02, nato lighttank 1.69 -> 1.37. So the anti-armour column as shipped systematically under-prices the western infantry missile and over-prices the Russian/Korean one — the opposite of the engine's own answer, in the column the whole exercise exists to get right. It is a two-line fix inside the existing penetration branch.

problems.item: scope — AREA 1 as an answer to the owner's request
problems.claim: "That is a PRIOR plus LEARNING… the two halves are one job and are designed together here."
problems.reality: This area contains no learning, no exploration, no outcome memory and no state of any kind. doctrine(fac, era) is a pure function of two static tables, cached forever, identical in match 1 and match 100 — so on the owner's first complaint ("tired of the game only repetition") it contributes literally nothing; it makes the commander smarter, not less repetitive. The critic's questions about bandits, 15-wave sample counts and attribution have no referent here, which is itself the finding. It is also inert at cold start by its own design (every modulated term sits behind an observed share, so nothing fires until the first sighting), and the floor mixture — the only thing that would deliver "start competent instead of ignorant" — is explicitly out of scope. So of the two things the owner asked for twice, this delivers the response half of the prior half. Worse for the sequel: DOCT is a frozen module-level cache with no per-commander copy and no blend point, so the learning half has nowhere to write. If Area 2 ends up multiplying a different coefficient, the two will compound rather than blend, and a prior with an inverted term (above) becomes the starting point a 15-sample estimator has no hope of unlearning.

problems.item: edits 3 and 5 — dm.heavy.at and dm.heavy.mbt, multiplied onto terms already conditioned by heatEdge(a.plate)  (js/ai.js:1599, 1607)
problems.claim: The modulator scales the response to an observed share, so it sharpens the adaptation rather than weakening it.
problems.reality: dm.heavy.at and dm.heavy.mbt re-encode "can my gun defeat a heavy plate", which counterMix already asks — against the OBSERVED plate — through heatEdge() at ai.js:1341, which is the fog-honest version of the same question. The prior's version uses an era-typical plate, so the stale fact keeps firing when the observed enemy is not a modern MBT. Worked example: KPA e20 against an observed 400 mm plate, heatEdge = 0.46 (the Chonma-ho's 365 mm is adequate there), so the mbt term is already only 0.16*(1-0.46) = 0.086 of armour — and the prior then cuts it again by 0.57, on the strength of a 738 mm plate nobody has seen. The two multiplications are the same signal, one of which is fogged and one of which is not. Either leave the two terms heatEdge already conditions alone, or use the observed plate inside the prior's heavy column — and the latter breaks the (faction, era) cache key, which is an honest argument for dropping these two edits rather than keeping them.

problems.item: "Nothing per-match ever enters it — no upgrades, no veterancy, no optics — so the key stays sound."
problems.claim: Excluding per-match state keeps the (faction, era) cache key correct.
problems.reality: The key is sound; the model is not. UPGRADES.ap ("Tungsten Penetrators", rules.js:259) gives +18% damage to every cannon and bullet warhead and nothing to heat (combat.js:134), and ai.js:3376 makes it the FIRST marginal upgrade the commander buys. The moment it completes, every gun term in the prior is 18% stale in exactly the gun-versus-missile dimension the prior exists to price, and the commander is still told to buy missiles. UPGRADES.optics (+15% weapon range, entities.js:206) likewise feeds the reach term. Both are OUR OWN upgrades — reading them is fog-legal and free; the key becomes fac|era|ap|optics.

problems.item: the zero-versus-air audit — "the only warheads on ground mounts that declare tgt.air are flak (108 weapons) and cannon (8)"
problems.claim: Starstreak/Stormer are the only zero-damage air weapons the derivation found.
problems.reality: Counts are wrong and the audit is incomplete. Measured: air-capable weapons are flak 334, he 73, cannon 15. CFG.DMG.he.air is 0.00 as well, so 73 air-capable weapons also do literally nothing to an aircraft — every navy's dual-purpose 76 mm and 57 mm (navgun_76 on LCS, Type 23, Type 45, Horizon, Sachsen, Project 22160, Type 056, Nampo, Tuo Chiang; navgun_57 on the minesweepers). That makes navalMix's own comment at ai.js:1386 ("the corvette brings navgun_76 at 8 tiles" as the cheap answer to aircraft) wrong today, in the same one-word way. The Starstreak finding itself is REAL and I confirmed it: dmgMult("cannon","air") === 0, gbr aa/spaag at e90/e00/e20 are the only hard zeros anywhere in the 8-faction x 6-era table, and the fallback holds — Sky Sabre (role sam) and the Typhoon are flak and unaffected, and no BUILDING has a zero-versus-air weapon, so the fixed SAM still works. Fix the weapon table first; keep the hard-zero rule as the general guard.

problems.item: prose facts that will live in the file as a comment
problems.claim: "NATO e60 costMul 1.06 accMul 1.07 rangeMul 1.08"; "the only he weapons in the entire ground order of battle are the twelve TEL ballistic rounds and the dmg-0 mine cargo shells".
problems.reality: rules.js:295 says accMul 1.06, not 1.07 (the computation used 1.06 — only the prose is wrong; I reproduced every published figure exactly). And there are 137 ground-capable he weapons with dmg > 0 in the tables. The operative claim is correct and I verified it — across all 8 factions and all 6 eras, every he weapon on the fifteen manoeuvre roles is a scat_* cargo shell with dmg 0 — but the sweeping version is not, and it is the version going into the file.

problems.claim: A module-level entry point so the manual can be printed from the console.
problems.reality: Its newCode is truncated in the submitted design (`return doctrine(fac, era || C`), so rule 5 cannot be checked on it — I cannot verify it repeats the anchor, closes the method, or keeps the object's commas intact. problems.item: effect size of the infantry column and the mg/mortar edits (7, 8)
problems.claim: "Modulated for consistency"; the 0.88-1.24 spread is a deliberate null result.
problems.reality: It is a null result in the stronger sense that it can almost never change a purchase. buildToward (ai.js:1737) normalises the mixture and takes the single largest gap, so only relative shares matter and the decision is a discrete argmax over five roles. End to end on the normalised queue, the mg/mortar/rifle modulators move a role by 0.3-1.1 points; across six factions x two pictures the first purchase changed in 3 of 8 cases and never because of an infantry modulator. Not harmful — but three of eleven edits are close to no-ops that a reader still has to verify, and the case for shipping them is weaker than the case for saying in the comment that the prior has nothing to say here.

missed: Verified and worth stating plainly: the derivation is honest and reproducible. I re-implemented doctValue/doctNorm/doctrine verbatim in jsc against js/util.js config.js facts.js rules.js eras.js heavyair.js generations.js and got the shipped modulator tables to the last digit — nato e20 at 0.77 / ifv 1.35 / lighttank 1.69, kpa ifv 1.80 / mbt 0.57, pact e60 ifv 1.80, gbr aa 0.00 / spaag 0.00, roc mbt 0.55 — and every raw per-1,000-credit figure quoted (Javelin 64.2, Abrams 22.7, Bradley 30.1, Stinger 130.8, MG Team 236.2 for the KPA). No faction/era pair throws or produces NaN across 48 combinations. Cost is the right order: cold build 1 ms in jsc including the 8-army norm, 88 ns a cached lookup.

Test [29] is safe, and for the reason given. The suite's commander is PACT at e20 (main.js:36 defaults opt-foe to pact; _behtest sets era e20 and never sets factions), whose modulators are at 0.97, tankdestroyer 1.09, mg 1.02 — all strictly positive, as is every value in the heavy and infantry sets for all 8 factions x 6 eras (the only zeros anywhere are gbr air). Each modulated term is coefficient x observed share x positive constant, and guard() tops up only rifle/mbt/ifv and never touches at/tankdestroyer/mg, so at2<at1, td2<td1, mg2>mg1 and the JSON inequality all hold by construction.

Cold start, answered directly since it was asked: at minute one the commander is byte-identical to today — every modulated term sits behind an observed share that is 0 while seenU is empty, so nothing fires. The regression is not at minute one, it is at FIRST CONTACT: the instant sArmour crosses 0.12 the light-tank inversion lands, and for NATO and the KPA the queue gets worse than today's deterministic version. That is the cold-start failure to watch for, one threshold later than the question expected.

The first-buy test is the one worth measuring in the browser: because buildToward is a greedy argmax, the honest measure of this change is not the weight vector but which unit actually comes out of the factory. Measured on the modelled queue, that changed in 3 of 8 faction/picture cases — kpa inf at->rifle, gbr and fra inf rifle->at, kpa veh mbt->spaag. Those five are the whole observable behavioural delta of eleven edits; they are what a human should watch for, and they are small enough that an A/B over a handful of matches will not separate them from noise.

A cheap way to keep the prior honest that the design did not consider: normalise the ADD terms against the era mean (which is right — I confirmed the within-army mean saturates the clamp at 1.80 for `at` in every army, exactly as the design says), but anchor the DISCOUNT terms to value(role)/max(value in set) within our own army. That single split fixes the fatal item, keeps every IFV case, and as a bonus removes the cross-army era norm from the two terms where the fog argument is least comfortable.

Nothing in this change reads an enemy object, map, tile, sighting, queue or cash — I checked the whole block. doctrine(fac, era) takes two strings and runs with no Game at all, which is how I ran it. The fog audit is sound as written.
